items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to prohibiting the manufacture and sale of personal care products and over-the-counter drugs containing synthetic plastic microbeads
items.lawCode: Add Art 37 Title 9 §§37-0901 - 37-0905, En Con L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4403

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the environmental conservation law, in
relation to prohibiting the manufacture and sale of personal care
products and over-the-counter drugs containing synthetic plastic
microbeads

PURPOSE:

The bill will prohibit the manufacture and sale of personal care
products and over-the-counter drugs containing synthetic plastic
microbeads.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends Article 37 of the environmental conservation law by
adding a new title 9 to read as follows "SYNTHETIC PLASTIC BEADS"
which:

1. Defines the term "over-the-counter drug", "personal care product",
"plastic", and "synthetic plastic microbead".

2. Sets the date upon which the manufacture for sale of a personal
care product, except for over-the-counter drugs, which contain
synthetic plastic microbeads is prohibited.

3. Sets the date upon which the acceptance of sale of a personal care
product, except for over-the-counter drugs, which contain synthetic
plastic microbeads is prohibited.

4. Sets the date upon which the manufacture for sale of
over-the-counter drugs that contain synthetic plastic microbeads is
prohibited.

5. Sets the date upon which the acceptance of sale of an
over-the-counter drugs that contain synthetic plastic microbeads is
prohibited.

6. This bill shall preempt any ordinance or resolution of a
municipality, county or any other local government, relating to
synthetic plastic microbeads.

Section 2 sets forth the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

This bill takes much needed steps to reduce plastic pollution in
waters across New York State. Microbeads are commonly found in many
different products including but not limited to facial scrubs, soaps,
shampoos and toothpastes. Quite often these microbeads are made of
plastics. Unfortunately due to the chemical composition of plastics
used these microbeads tend to absorb various toxins.

One would expect that these microbeads to be filtered out in sewage
treatment plants but because of their small size and buoyancy they
escape treatment by sewage plants and eventually are discharged into
our rivers, lakes and oceans.


Microbeads are often mistaken for food by small fish and wildlife. Due
to biomagnification the level of toxins existent in an organism
increases as we move higher in trophic levels, essentially up the food
chain. Not only do these microbeads pose a potential threat to our
bodies of water, but because of biomagnifications, higher levels of
toxins are accumulating in fish and wildlife. which additionally poses
harm to humans that may consume these animals.

It makes sense for New York to take action and prevent the continued
use of microbeads in order to protect our aquatic environments,
wildlife and public health.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.
